# s404 — The relay ledger has a waiting phase, so a run waiting on the owner is not stale

**Findings:**  · **Size:** S · **Tree:**

**2026-10-26** — Verified: relay-run step --phase wait [--waiting-on owner|approval] is written as a start event carrying waiting_on, so older slicers fold it as a heartbeat instead of refusing the ledger as corrupt. A run with a waiting step is never stale, relay-run list shows it (text 'waiting owner', 1 waiting; JSON step.waiting_on and counts.waiting, additive), and land refuses it with run_active. A later start, done or fail ends the wait; --waiting-on without --phase wait is usage. Full suite 2701 tests OK, slicer check passes.

trust: unverified; by: Jon Robbins

**Not in this slice:**

## Why

`relay-run` marks a run stale 30 minutes after the last step event (`STALE_AFTER`, `src/slicer/relayrun.py:49`). A run that waits for owner approval or an owner answer is not stale. ork's S78 waited at awaiting-approval and showed as "stale ... 23m", so it looked dead (ork S138, 2026-10-26). `slicer land` also refuses `run_active` only while a run is not stale, so staleness carries meaning.

## Implement

Add `--phase wait` (with an optional `--waiting-on owner|approval`) to `relay-run step`. A waiting step never makes its run stale, and `relay-run list` shows it as waiting. Align with s396's ask and answer.
